excerpt: Kelviq is a merchant of record and billing platform for SaaS, AI and digital products: payments, global tax, subscriptions, usage-based billing, license keys and payouts for 3.5% + 40¢ per transaction. Fees, how it compares with Stripe and Paddle, and alternatives.
content:
Kelviq is a monetisation platform for software, AI and digital products. As the merchant of record it is the legal seller, so it collects and remits sales tax, VAT and GST, and handles fraud, chargebacks and compliance on your behalf. On top of payments and checkout in local currencies, it offers subscriptions, usage-based billing that meters events such as AI tokens or API calls in real time, credits, feature entitlements tied to plans, digital file delivery and license keys. Pricing models can be flat, per seat, per token, tiered, credit-based or hybrid, and changed without code changes.

Kelviq charges per successful transaction with no setup or monthly fee: 2.9% + 40¢ on your first $5,000 of sales, then 3.5% + 40¢, plus 1.5% for non-US cards and 0.7% on recurring charges. It uses Stripe for core payment processing, pays out on a rolling seven-day basis, and the team says individuals can sign up without a company, including in India through Stripe Connect. It can help migrate products, customers and subscriptions from Stripe, Paddle or Lemon Squeezy.

Kelviq was founded by Alok Vats, Sachin Neravath and Geo Jacob; the founders previously built ParityDeals and the open-source lightGallery. It launched on Product Hunt on 12 May 2026 and finished #1 for the day with 520 upvotes and 84 comments.

We have not tested Kelviq ourselves. This page brings together Kelviq's website, pricing and about pages, its Product Hunt page and launch discussion, and says where each fact comes from.

paragraphs: Sachin Neravath says the team kept seeing the same problem through their earlier product, ParityDeals: adding a payment gateway is easy, but building everything around it is not. Charging for features, seats, usage or AI tokens usually means webhook listeners, subscription tables, usage tracking and feature flags, and pricing ends up tied to your code.

Kelviq is meant to replace that with one system: Kelviq as merchant of record for tax in 100+ countries, any pricing model configured in minutes, digital delivery and license keys, and real-time metering of usage.

use_cases: Selling a SaaS or AI product worldwide without registering for foreign tax IDs
Charging for AI tokens, API calls or compute with real-time metering
Selling downloads or software with automatic license keys
Changing plans, limits and feature access without code deployments
Moving from Stripe, Paddle or Lemon Squeezy to a single billing stack

fit: sell software, AI or digital products to customers in many countries
need usage-based or hybrid pricing without building metering yourself
are an individual founder, including in India, who wants a merchant of record without a company
not_fit: sell mobile app subscriptions through Apple or Google: in-app purchases are not supported yet
only need payment processing and handle tax yourself: plain Stripe is cheaper per transaction
need automatic tracking of AI model vendor price changes: the team said that is manual for now

pricing.intro: Kelviq has no plans or monthly fee; it charges per successful transaction. Figures are from Kelviq's pricing page in US dollars.

plans.name: First $5,000 of sales
plans.detail: Applies until total processed volume reaches $5,000

plans.name: Standard
plans.detail: Payments, merchant of record, tax, billing, metering and entitlements; unlimited seats, no setup or monthly fee

notes: Extra fees: +1.5% for international (non-US) cards and +0.7% on recurring subscription charges.
Payouts on a rolling 7-day basis; Enterprise partners can negotiate faster schedules.
API calls and metering events are not charged.

alternatives.intro: Product Hunt lists Polar, Dodo Payments, Paddle and Stripe among Kelviq's alternatives. Review scores are Product Hunt users' own; check each provider's pricing page for current fees.

items.name: Paddle
items.what: Merchant of record for digital products and SaaS
items.difference: The established merchant of record; Kelviq leads with usage metering and entitlements for AI products.

items.name: Polar
items.difference: Open source and developer-focused; Kelviq is closed source with built-in license keys and migration help.

items.name: Dodo Payments
items.what: Payments and billing for AI, SaaS and digital products
items.difference: A close like-for-like merchant of record; compare fees and supported payout countries.

alternatives.more: Product Hunt also lists Stripe and PaymentKit.

faq.a: No monthly fee. 2.9% + 40¢ per transaction on your first $5,000 of sales, then 3.5% + 40¢, plus 1.5% on non-US cards and 0.7% on recurring charges.

faq.q: Is Kelviq a merchant of record?
faq.a: Yes. Kelviq is the legal seller and handles global sales tax, VAT, GST, fraud and chargebacks.

faq.q: Can I use Kelviq as an individual in India?
faq.a: The team says yes: you do not need a company, and payouts go to your bank account through Stripe Connect.

faq.q: Does it support usage-based billing for AI products?
faq.a: Yes. It meters events such as tokens or API calls in real time and supports credits, overages and hybrid pricing.

faq.q: Can I migrate from Stripe or Paddle?
faq.a: Kelviq says it can migrate products, plans, customers and subscriptions, and saved payment methods where the old provider supports PCI-compliant migration.
Product Hunt lists Polar, Dodo Payments, PaymentKit, Paddle and Stripe.
